title: NIO Sells 30% Stake in Battery-Swap Unit NIO Power to Geely for $2B+
detail: NIO has agreed to sell a 30% stake in its battery-swap subsidiary NIO Power to Geely for over $2 billion (RMB 16 billion), marking a major consolidation in China's EV battery-swap infrastructure sector. The deal values NIO Power — which operates China's largest network of automated battery-swapping stations — at roughly $6.7 billion. Geely's participation brings one of China's largest automakers into NIO's swap ecosystem, potentially accelerating the standardization of battery-swap technology and expanding the network's reach to Geely-branded EVs. The transaction underscores growing investor confidence in battery-swap as a viable fast-energy-replenishment model, offering an alternative to conventional DC fast charging for high-utilization fleet and consumer markets.

title: US Clean Energy Jobs Fall for First Time Since Pandemic
detail: US clean energy employment declined for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, signaling a potential slowdown in the sector's previously robust job growth. The drop raises concerns about the durability of clean energy's labor market expansion, which had been driven by federal investment incentives and accelerating renewable deployment. The pullback may reflect economic headwinds, policy uncertainty, or a maturation effect in certain segments of the sector as initial buildout surges stabilize.
